name: Plus Minus Tree
description: You are given a tree $$$T$$$ with $$$n$$$ vertices, rooted$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ at vertex $$$1$$$. Each vertex $$$v$$$ is assigned an initial weight $$$ a_v \in \{ -1, 0, +1 \} $$$. For each vertex with weight $$$0$$$, you have to assign a new weight, either $$$-1$$$ or $$$+1$$$. Let $$$x_v$$$ be the final weight of vertex $$$v$$$. For vertex $$$v$$$, let $$$T_v$$$ be the set of nodes in the subtree$$$^{\text{†}}$$$ of vertex $$$v$$$. The cost of vertex $$$v$$$ is defined as $$$$$$ S_v = \left| \sum_{u \in T_v}{x_u} \right|.$$$$$$ The total cost of the tree is defined as the sum of costs over all vertices. Find the minimum possible total cost of the tree after assigning the weights of all vertices with zero initial weight. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A tree is a connected graph without cycles. A rooted tree is a tree where one vertex is special and called the root. $$$^{\text{†}}$$$A subtree of vertex $$$v$$$ is the subgraph consisting of $$$v$$$, all its descendants, and all the edges between them. A descendant of vertex $$$v$$$ is any vertex $$$u$$$ for which $$$v$$$ is an ancestor. No vertex is its own descendant. An ancestor of vertex $$$v$$$ is any vertex on the simple path from $$$v$$$ to the root, including the root, but not including $$$v$$$. The root has no ancestors.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$), denoting the number of vertices in the tree. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$-1 \le a_i \le 1$$$). Each of the next $$$n-1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$), denoting the nodes connected with an edge of the tree. It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print the minimum total cost of the tree.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2258F — Plus Minus Tree [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
